description: Relocate five legacy root-level bare-verb / misnamed command paths to their owning resource groups (project status, system logs, project use single-entry, notification setup, server info), drop legacy paths with no aliases, and converge the root command layer to resources + the single `mo info` exception.

tasks.title: Relocate mo status to mo project status
tasks.description: Move the legacy root-level status factory (BuildStatusCommand in MohistCliCommands.cs, handler api.PrintGetAsync("/api/status?all=true")) into ProjectCommands as a new BuildStatus, register it under the project command group as a peer of list/create/show/use/delete/workflow, and delete the root registration (MohistCliCommands.cs root Build line + the private BuildStatusCommand method). The handler, endpoint string, and rendering stay byte-identical. Add a new CliProjectStatusCommandSpecs covering: project --help lists status; project status --help advertises no positional project arg and no --project/--project-id flags; project status hits GET /api/status?all=true and exits 0; server-unreachable emits the legacy guidance and exits non-zero; and the legacy `mo status` no longer resolves at the root (exits non-zero) per the no-alias decision.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo project --help` lists `status` alongside list, create, show, use, delete, workflow.
`mo project status --help` advertises no positional `project` argument and no `--project` / `--project-id` flags.
`mo project status` issues GET /api/status?all=true, renders the response identically to legacy `mo status`, and exits 0.
`mo project status` against an unreachable server emits the same server-unavailable guidance as legacy `mo status` and exits non-zero.
`mo status` fails to resolve at the root and exits non-zero (no alias retained).
New spec file CliProjectStatusCommandSpecs.cs passes; existing CLI test suite still green; build treats warnings as errors.
tasks.output: Relocated `mo project status` command (MohistCliCommands.Project.cs) + removed root status registration (MohistCliCommands.cs) + new packages/cli/tests/.../CliProjectStatusCommandSpecs.cs
tasks.notes: Per design D2: mechanical factory-method relocation, handler untouched. The legacy `mo status` root path is removed outright (D1: no aliases). No server/endpoint change.

tasks.title: Relocate mo logs to mo system logs and reframe system group as application diagnostics
tasks.description: Move the legacy root-level logs factory (BuildLogsCommand in MohistCliCommands.cs, handler api.PrintGetAsync("/api/logs/tail")) into SystemCommands as a new BuildLogs, register it under the system command group, and delete the root registration. Update the system group description so `mo system --help` explicitly identifies its `logs` as application logs (Mohist server's own log tail) and distinguishes them from the operational logs surfaced by `mo server logs` (systemd journal / scheduled-task output). Handler, endpoint, and rendering stay byte-identical. Add a new CliSystemLogsCommandSpecs covering: system --help lists logs; the group description records the application-vs-operational distinction; system logs hits GET /api/logs/tail and exits 0; server-unreachable guidance + non-zero exit; and the legacy `mo logs` no longer resolves at the root.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo system --help` lists `logs` as a subcommand.
The `system` group description identifies its logs as application logs and distinguishes them from the operational logs of `mo server logs`.
`mo system logs` issues GET /api/logs/tail, renders the response identically to legacy `mo logs`, and exits 0.
`mo system logs` against an unreachable server emits the same guidance as legacy `mo logs` and exits non-zero.
`mo logs` fails to resolve at the root and exits non-zero (no alias retained).
New spec file CliSystemLogsCommandSpecs.cs passes; existing CLI test suite still green.
tasks.output: Relocated `mo system logs` command (MohistCliCommands.System.cs) + updated system group description + removed root logs registration (MohistCliCommands.cs) + new CliSystemLogsCommandSpecs.cs
tasks.notes: Per design D3: the system group must not be left empty after T-005 moves `info` out; this task moves `logs` in and reframes the group as application diagnostics. The application-vs-operational distinction in the group description is a hard spec requirement.

tasks.title: Remove duplicate root mo use so mo project use is the single entry
tasks.description: Delete the duplicate root-level use factory (BuildUseCommand in MohistCliCommands.cs and its root Build registration line). The surviving `mo project use` (ProjectCommands.BuildUse, same UseProjectAsync handler) becomes the only entry. Handler, endpoint (POST /api/projects/{id}/use), activeProjectId persistence, confirmation text, and error/guidance text stay unchanged. Add/extend tests covering: `mo --help` no longer lists `use`; `mo use <project>` fails to resolve and exits non-zero; `mo project use <identifier>` still resolves the identifier, POSTs, persists activeProjectId, prints `Active project: <name> (<id>)`, exits 0; and failure/rejection leaves local project state unmodified and exits non-zero.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo --help` does not list `use` as a top-level subcommand.
`mo use <project>` fails to resolve at the root and exits non-zero (no alias retained).

`mo project use <identifier>` keeps its behavior: resolves the identifier, issues POST /api/projects/<identifier>/use with empty body, writes activeProjectId to local project state, prints `Active project: <name> (<id>)`, and exits 0.
On server rejection or unreachable, `mo project use` emits the same error/guidance text as before, exits non-zero, and does not modify local project state.
Tests pass; build treats warnings as errors.
tasks.output: Removed root `mo use` registration + private factory (MohistCliCommands.cs); surviving `mo project use` unchanged; tests asserting single-entry behavior + legacy `mo use` non-resolution
tasks.notes: This is deletion of a duplicate entry, not a behavior change — `mo project use` already shares the same UseProjectAsync handler. Per design D1 the legacy root path is removed with no alias.

tasks.title: Rename root notify group to notification resource group
tasks.description: Rename the root command group `notify` to the resource noun `notification` by changing the group-name literal in NotifyCommands.Build (and the XML doc comment). The `setup` subcommand, its guided flow (probe Hermes health, validate --platform, generate signing secret, prompt before overwrite, write Mohist:Notifications:Hermes, print the hermes subscribe command), and all flags (--health-base default http://127.0.0.1:8644, --webhook-url, --platform, --deliver-chat-id) with their defaults, validation, exit codes, output wording, and config-path/seam overrides stay byte-identical. Keep the NotifyCommands class name (internal, no command-surface impact) to minimize churn. Rewrite the existing CliNotifySetupCommandSpecs.cs: replace every ["notify",...] args array with ["notification",...], rename NotifyRoot_Help_ListsSetupSubcommand to NotificationRoot_Help_ListsSetupSubcommand, and add an assertion that `mo notify` no longer resolves at the root.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo --help` lists `notification` and does not list `notify`.
`mo notification --help` lists `setup`.
`mo notification setup --help` documents --health-base (default http://127.0.0.1:8644), --webhook-url, --platform, --deliver-chat-id with descriptions matching the legacy `mo notify setup --help`.
`mo notification setup` happy path writes Mohist:Notifications:Hermes (WebhookUrl, Secret, EnabledTypes) and prints the same `hermes webhook subscribe mohist ...` command as legacy, exiting 0.

`mo notification setup` probe failure prints the same `Hermes webhook platform is not started.` guidance (with docs/hermes-notifications.md pointer), writes no config file, and exits non-zero without a stack trace.
`mo notify setup` fails to resolve at the root under the legacy name and exits non-zero (no alias retained).
Updated CliNotifySetupCommandSpecs.cs passes; build treats warnings as errors.
tasks.output: Renamed notification group (Notify.cs group literal + XML doc) + rewritten CliNotifySetupCommandSpecs.cs (notify→notification args) + legacy `mo notify` non-resolution assertion
tasks.notes: Per design D2 the NotifyCommands class name is kept (only the group literal changes) to avoid rewriting all static references like NotifyCommands.HealthProbeOverride in tests. All setup logic is static and decoupled from the group name.

tasks.title: Relocate mo system info to mo server info
tasks.description: Move BuildInfo out of SystemCommands (System.cs) into ServerCommands (Server.cs) as a new BuildInfo, registering it under the server command group as a peer of health/install/update/start/stop/restart/status/logs/uninstall. The handler (api.PrintSystemInfoAsync(mode)) stays byte-identical: still issues GET /api/system/info, renders the same six sections (Identity, Source, Install, Update, Services, Paths), supports -o/--output (default table, accepts table|json), and renders the same degraded-mode output (CLI-local version line + `Server is not running. Start with: mo server start` guidance) when unreachable. The command description must distinguish it from `mo info` (CLI-local). Rewrite the existing CliSystemInfoCommandSpecs.cs: replace every ["system","info",...] args array with ["server","info",...], rename System_Help_ListsInfoSubcommand to Server_Help_ListsInfoSubcommand, add System_Help_NoLongerListsInfo, and add an assertion that `mo system info` no longer resolves.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo server --help` lists `info` alongside health, install, update, start, stop, restart, status, logs, uninstall.
`mo system --help` does not list `info`.
`mo server info` against a running server issues GET /api/system/info and renders the Identity, Source, Install, Update, Services, Paths sections identically to legacy `mo system info`, exiting 0.
`mo server info -o json` renders the diagnostics envelope as JSON matching legacy `mo system info -o json`; default `-o table` matches the legacy default.
`mo server info` against an unreachable server renders the same degraded-mode output (CLI-local version line + `Server is not running. Start with: mo server start`) and exits 0.
`mo server info --help` description identifies it as server-side system diagnostics and distinguishes it from `mo info` (CLI-local environment).
`mo system info` fails to resolve and exits non-zero (no alias retained).
Updated CliSystemInfoCommandSpecs.cs passes; build treats warnings as errors.
tasks.output: Relocated `mo server info` command (Server.cs) + removed BuildInfo from System.cs + rewritten CliSystemInfoCommandSpecs.cs (system info→server info args, class name retained)
tasks.notes: Keep the CliSystemInfoCommandSpecs class name (only change args) to preserve git blame per design Risks/Trade-offs. `mo info` (the controlled CLI-local exception) is not touched by this task.

tasks.title: Converge root command shape: guard tests, doc sync, alias-policy record
tasks.description: After all five migrations land, add the cross-cutting root-command-shape guard and sync all documentation. (1) Add a new CliRootCommandShapeSpecs.cs: `mo --help` lists project/system/server/notification and the single `info` exception, and does not list status/logs/use/notify; each legacy path (mo status, mo logs, mo use <x>, mo notify setup, mo system info) fails to resolve and exits non-zero; `mo info` output and exit code are unchanged vs. pre-change. (2) Update CliReferenceDocsSpecs.cs:78-123 expectations from the legacy paths to the new canonical paths. (3) Update docs/cli-reference.md: remove the five gap-table rows, update the Project / System / Notification / Server command-group sections to the new paths, and refresh the `mo --help` example to list only resources + `info`. (4) Sweep all other docs prose (docs/concepts.md, docs/getting-started.md, docs/runner.md, docs/troubleshooting.md, docs/issues.md, docs/hermes-notifications.md) replacing legacy paths with canonical ones; verify with `rg --fixed-strings 'mo status|mo logs|mo use|mo notify|mo system info' docs/`. (5) Post an issue comment recording the uniform alias policy decision (D1: all five legacy paths removed, no aliases retained, rationale: project declares no version compatibility) to satisfy the root-command-shape alias-policy requirement.
acceptanceCriteria: New CliRootCommandShapeSpecs.cs passes: `mo --help` lists only resource/resource-group commands plus `info`, and does not list status/logs/use/notify.
Each legacy path (`mo status`, `mo logs`, `mo use <x>`, `mo notify setup`, `mo system info`) fails to resolve and exits non-zero in the guard spec.
`mo info` output and exit code are byte-identical to the pre-change state (controlled exception preserved).
CliReferenceDocsSpecs.cs passes with updated expectations asserting the new canonical paths.
docs/cli-reference.md gap table no longer contains rows for mo status, mo logs, mo use, mo notify setup, or mo system info; its command-group sections and `mo --help` example reflect the new paths.
`rg --fixed-strings 'mo status|mo logs|mo use|mo notify|mo system info' docs/` returns no legacy-path references after the sweep.
An issue comment records the uniform no-alias policy decision and its rationale.
Full CLI test suite green; build treats warnings as errors.
tasks.output: New CliRootCommandShapeSpecs.cs + updated CliReferenceDocsSpecs.cs + synced docs/cli-reference.md + swept docs/*.md + issue comment recording the alias-policy decision
tasks.notes: This is the convergence task that closes the loop: the root-shape guard only holds once all five migrations are in, and doc/code sync is done as one cohesive sweep per design D5. The alias-policy comment is mandatory per root-command-shape spec (D1 pre-decided: no aliases, uniform).
